result.title: BReD: Block Replay Dithering for Stable Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States
result.summary: Low-bit storage of optimizer states can substantially reduce the memory footprint of large-scale training. In practice, however, these states are not quantized once: at every training step, they are dequantized, updated, requantized, and written back. This iterative quantization pipeline can destabilize training. We identify a failure mode behind this instability: for states updated via exponential moving averages (EMAs), quantization errors are recursively fed into subsequent updates. As a result, biased errors accumulate over time while high-variance errors are amplified, particularly when the EMA decay factor is close to 1. To address this error accumulation, we propose BReD (Block Replay Dithering), a method that reduces rounding bias and controls rounding variance during quantization. BReD adapts classical subtractive dithering to optimizer-state quantization by combining deterministic seed replay with block-wise shared dither values, avoiding auxiliary random-tensor storage and per-element dither values generation. Across the default pretraining settings (five optimizers at 120M; AdamW and Muon at 1.1B and 3.4B model) and supervised fine-tuning (AdamW and Muon at 7B model), 4-bit BReD closely matches training with full-precision optimizer states, with PPL shifts $\leq0.5$ in pretraining and $\leq0.2$ in fine-tuning and average downstream performance changes within 0.7 points. Moreover, 3-bit BReD preserves stable convergence in the evaluated settings, offering a more aggressive alternative. Our implementation of BReD is available at: https://github.com/ZhanHeshen/BReD

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出低比特优化器状态在每步「反量化—更新—再量化」循环中会把量化误差递归反馈进 EMA 更新，导致偏差累积与高方差放大（衰减因子接近 1 时尤甚），并提出 BReD：用块级共享抖动加确定性种子重放来压低舍入偏差与方差，在 120M 至 7B 的预训练与微调中使 4-bit 状态接近全精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「递归状态更新中误差持续累积」的分析与抖动、误差反馈手段，可能可供核查 loop/迭代式 latent 推理状态反复更新时的漂移与信息保真问题，但与视觉证据使用无直接联系。
